9637900d-c713-485d-ac8a-d889eed65cfa.name: PCA - Shared - Host - Consumed pct of DRAM
9637900d-c713-485d-ac8a-d889eed65cfa.description: OBJECT: Host. UNIT: percent. Total DRAM footprint (hot + cold) as a percent of installed DRAM (the DRAM tier). Does NOT compute at Cluster scope - the DRAM-tier denominator does not roll up (verified live; cluster reads require child-aggregation). Activation-readiness for tiering (cold pages offload ~80% consumed) AND, for WTPC, the capacity utilization corridor read as a saturation ceiling at high-SLA postures.

e937675a-3a17-4305-9298-2382a906d5b9.name: PCA - MemTier - Host - Recoverable Cold DRAM GB
e937675a-3a17-4305-9298-2382a906d5b9.description: UPPER BOUND on the DRAM currently holding COLD pages (consumed but not active) - i.e. the memory tiering would relocate to NVMe, freeing DRAM. The ACTIONABLE ranking metric: sort candidates by this. It is an UPPER BOUND because pinned memory (latency-sensitive VMs, DirectPath/passthrough, vGPU, SR-IOV) is counted as cold here yet cannot tier; cross-check against mem|reservedCapacity_average and the VM-type exclusion list before trusting the figure on a given host.

860ddab7-816c-452f-ad99-c5bd61ec604e.name: PCA - MemTier - Host - Active pct of DRAM
860ddab7-816c-452f-ad99-c5bd61ec604e.description: The active working set as a percentage of installed DRAM capacity (the DRAM tier) - the AUTHORITATIVE Memory Tiering selection gate. Per vSphere best-practices, good candidates have active memory between 0% and 50% of DRAM. LOWER = better candidate (more cold headroom that can tier to NVMe). Denominator is the DRAM tier, NOT mem|totalCapacity_average (which on a tiered host is DRAM+NVMe and understates the ratio). GATE ON THE 95TH PERCENTILE over a representative window (peak working set) via the view transformation - the mean hides the peak a safety gate must size for.

89a9cb19-ad0d-4fdd-ab01-b7bb4401bd28.name: PCA - MemTier - Host - NVMe Tier Used GB
89a9cb19-ad0d-4fdd-ab01-b7bb4401bd28.description: HOST metric (HostSystem). Post-activation engagement signal: memory currently served from the NVMe tier (mem:NVMe|tier.usage, MB, shown as GB). Over 0 = tiering is actively offloading cold pages to NVMe; 0 = enabled-but-dormant or not configured. Pair with Consumed pct of DRAM (the ~80 pct trigger). Requires vSphere 8.0U3+/9.x with NVMe tiering configured. UNIT: GB.

dd92fb78-1076-44e5-bedc-5123a26b72fb.name: PCA - MemTier - Host - Actual Tiering Uplift GB
dd92fb78-1076-44e5-bedc-5123a26b72fb.description: OBJECT: HostSystem. UNIT: GB. Memory a host has ACTUALLY gained from its configured NVMe tier (mem:NVMe|memory_tier_size), reflecting that host's real Mem.TierNVMePct ratio. The deployed-reality counterpart to Tiering Uplift GB (which projects the gain at a uniform planning ratio); a mixed-ratio fleet reports accurately here. Blank on a host with no NVMe tier configured.

5de20df1-4648-42cd-9d16-7c1359d43c18.name: PCA - MemTier - Host - Reserved Memory GB
5de20df1-4648-42cd-9d16-7c1359d43c18.description: OBJECT: HostSystem. UNIT: GB. Pinned memory on the host - reservations guarantee physical DRAM, so this memory cannot tier to NVMe. Read it as a QUALIFIER on Recoverable Cold DRAM: up to this much of a host's cold DRAM is pinned and will not actually reclaim, so a host with high reserved memory reclaims less than its Recoverable Cold suggests. mem|reservedCapacity_average / 1048576.
